elements.element: Preferred: no liquidated damages payable by Customer (PB) under the Agreement
elements.evidence: "PB will pay SFJ, within [***] of the date of termination, an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination"; "shall be in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have"

elements.element: Preferred: no penalty payable by Customer (PB)
elements.evidence: the punitive multiplier is deleted \u2014 "an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred" replaces "three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs"

elements.element: Fallback: any Customer termination payment is structured as an early-termination fee
elements.evidence: payment is framed as consideration "in exchange for purchasing the Trial Data Package", measured by SFJ's Development Costs, not as an early-termination fee

elements.element: Fallback: that fee is capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "an amount equal to the Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination" \u2014 no monetary or 3-month cap

elements.element: Fallback: the capped fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "the payment by PB to SFJ of the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2 shall be in lieu of any claim for damages"

reasons: The edit removes the treble multiplier, which cures the penal character, but a fixed termination payment measured by all of SFJ's Development Costs and expressly standing "in lieu of any claim for damages" remains a liquidated amount payable by Customer, so the locked preferred level (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) is not achieved on the operative text.
The fallback is also unmet: the surviving amount is uncapped by reference to 3 months' fees and is not structured as an early-termination fee.

To reach preferred, delete or carve PB's termination payment out of the Section 14.4.2 in-lieu-of-damages mechanic (or delete the payment obligation); to reach fallback, insert an express cap (e.g. "but in no event more than three (3) months' fees") as the sole liquidated amount.
Minimality and intent are satisfied: a single number/operator was changed, no new exceptions or undefined terms were introduced, and the purchase and exclusive-remedy mechanics remain effective.
